examples.en: I meet my family face to face after a long time.
The two people met face to face in the meeting room for the first time.
I was scared to face the other person in the accident.
I want to talk in person, not online.
I will meet the boss in person tomorrow.
You need the courage to face a hard reality.

explain: '만나다'는 어디서나 쓰지만 '대면하다'는 직접 얼굴을 마주 본다는 점을 강조해요. '비대면'의 반대말로 뉴스와 회사에서 자주 들려요. '~을/를 대면하다'로 써요.
explain_en: '만나다' works anywhere, but '대면하다' stresses meeting face to face in person. You hear it a lot in news and at work as the opposite of '비대면' (non-face-to-face). It takes an object: '~을/를 대면하다'.

examples.en: The players walk in, lined up in ranks.
The students formed a line on the playground.

examples.ko: 앞 대열에 서 있는 사람이 우리 선생님이에요.
examples.en: The person standing in the front line is our teacher.

examples.ko: 마라톤 대열 맨 뒤에서 천천히 뛰었어요.
examples.en: I ran slowly at the very back of the marathon pack.
My friend suddenly slipped out of the line.

examples.ko: 비가 와도 응원 대열은 흩어지지 않았어요.
examples.en: Even in the rain, the cheering crowd did not scatter.

explain: '줄'은 일상에서 두루 쓰고, '대열'은 행진이나 행사, 큰 무리처럼 질서 있게 늘어선 사람들에게 써요. '선진국 대열'처럼 어떤 집단이나 수준을 비유할 때도 나와요.

phrases.example: 저도 오늘부터 취업 준비생 대열에 합류했어요.
phrases.nuance_ko: 어떤 무리나 흐름에 새로 들어가 함께하게 될 때 써요. 실제 줄이 아니라 비유로 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when you newly become part of a group or trend. It is figurative, not about a real line.

explain_en: '줄' is the everyday word for a line. '대열' is used for orderly groups such as marches, events, or large crowds. It also works figuratively, as in '선진국 대열' (the ranks of advanced countries).

examples.en: The child skates through the park on roller skates.

examples.ko: 공사장에서 큰 롤러가 땅을 평평하게 눌러요.
examples.en: At the construction site, a big roller flattens the ground.
Every weekend I go skating with my friend.

examples.ko: 이 롤러는 바퀴가 너무 작아서 불안해요.
examples.en: These skates have such small wheels that they feel unsafe.

examples.ko: 벽은 롤러로 칠하는 게 훨씬 빨라요.
examples.en: Painting a wall with a roller is much faster.
I am more used to a bicycle than to skates.

explain: '롤러'는 롤러스케이트를 줄여 부르기도 하고, 그때는 신을 때 '신다', 탈 때 '타다'를 써요. 공사 장비나 페인트 도구를 말할 때는 '도로 롤러', '페인트 롤러'처럼 앞말을 붙여야 헷갈리지 않아요.
explain_en: '롤러' can be short for roller skates, and then you use '신다' (wear) or '타다' (ride). For construction equipment or paint tools, add a word first, like '도로 롤러' or '페인트 롤러', so it is clear.

examples.ko: 지난 시험의 실수를 이번에 만회하고 싶어요.
examples.en: I want to make up for my mistake on the last test this time.
Our team made up the points in the second half.

examples.ko: 늦잠 잔 시간을 만회하려고 빨리 걸었어요.
examples.en: I walked fast to make up for the time I lost oversleeping.
Isn't there a way to make up for the loss?
A goal came that made up for the conceded point.

examples.ko: 이번 달 매출로 지난달 적자를 만회해요.
examples.en: We cover last month's deficit with this month's sales.

explain: '회복하다'는 나빠진 몸이나 상태가 원래대로 돌아올 때 쓰고, '만회하다'는 실수·손해·뒤처진 점수를 다시 채울 때 써요. '실수를 만회하다', '점수를 만회하다'처럼 메워야 할 부정적인 것과 같이 나와요.
explain_en: '회복하다' is for a body or condition returning to normal. '만회하다' is for making up a mistake, loss, or deficit in score. It pairs with something negative to fill in, like '실수를 만회하다' or '점수를 만회하다'.

examples.en: My younger sibling pushed me out the door.

examples.ko: 새 건물이 옛 가게를 밀어내고 들어섰어요.
examples.en: A new building pushed out the old shop and took its place.
I pushed the hot pot aside and sat down.
The baby keeps pushing the spoon out of its mouth.

examples.ko: 약한 사람을 밀어내는 건 좋지 않아요.
examples.en: It is not good to push weaker people aside.
The wind pushed the clouds far away.

explain: '밀다'는 힘을 줘서 움직이는 동작 전체이고, '밀어내다'는 밀어서 어떤 자리에서 없애거나 쫓아내는 느낌이 강해요. '밀치다'는 한 번 확 미는 동작이라 달라요. 경쟁에서 누군가의 자리를 빼앗는다는 비유로도 써요.
explain_en: '밀다' is any pushing motion; '밀어내다' pushes something away from its place, with a feel of removing or driving out. '밀치다' is a single sharp shove. It can also mean taking someone's spot in a competition.

examples.ko: 상급 반으로 올라가려면 시험을 봐야 해요.
examples.en: To move up to the higher class, you have to take a test.

examples.ko: 이 책은 초보자에게 상급 수준이라 어려워요.
examples.en: This book is at an advanced level, so it is hard for beginners.

examples.ko: 형은 저보다 두 학년 위인 상급생이에요.
examples.en: My older brother is an upperclassman two grades above me.
Please inquire at the higher authority.
You should listen carefully to your superior's instructions.
It is expensive because the meat is top quality.

explain: 반대말은 '하급'이에요. 한국어 수업에서 학습 수준은 '초급-중급-고급'을 더 많이 쓰고, '상급'은 학년·직급·기관·품질처럼 위아래 단계를 말할 때 자주 써요. '상급반', '상급자', '상급 기관'으로 외워 두세요.
explain_en: The opposite is '하급'. For learner level, '초급-중급-고급' is more common; '상급' is used for school years, ranks, institutions, and quality. Remember it in '상급반', '상급자', and '상급 기관'.

examples.en: I saw an otter for the first time at the zoo.

examples.ko: 수달 한 마리가 물속에서 헤엄치고 있어요.
examples.en: An otter is swimming in the water.
Otters catch and eat fish.
In Korea, otters are a protected animal.
I got a cute otter doll as a present.
The otter is an animal that swims in clear rivers.

explain: 강과 하천에 사는 동물이에요. 바다에 사는 비슷한 동물은 '해달'이라고 불러서 서로 달라요. 한국에서는 천연기념물이라 뉴스에서 '수달 발견'처럼 나오기도 해요.
explain_en: An animal that lives in rivers and streams. The similar sea-dwelling animal is called '해달' (sea otter), so the two differ. In Korea it is a natural monument, so news sometimes reports '수달 발견' (otter sighted).

examples.en: Our team earned three league points.
You get three points for a win and one for a draw.

examples.ko: 승점이 같으면 골 득실로 순위를 정해요.
examples.en: If the points are tied, rank is decided by goal difference.
The gap in points narrowed in the last match.
We are ahead by one point.

examples.ko: 승점을 많이 쌓아서 올해는 순위가 많이 올랐어요.
examples.en: We piled up many points, so our ranking rose a lot this year.

explain: 축구 같은 리그 경기에서 이기면 3점, 비기면 1점을 주는 점수예요. 한 경기에서 넣은 점수는 '득점', 리그 순위를 정하는 점수는 '승점'이라서 둘이 달라요. 스포츠 뉴스와 중계에서 자주 들려요.
explain_en: In league sports like soccer, a win gives 3 and a draw 1. Goals scored in one match are '득점', while '승점' is what decides the league standings, so the two differ. You hear it often in sports news and broadcasts.

examples.en: My eyes feel gritty because my eyeballs are dry.
The doctor examined the eyeball carefully.

examples.ko: 안구 운동을 하면 눈이 덜 피곤해요.
examples.en: Doing eye exercises makes your eyes less tired.

examples.ko: 안구 건조증이 있으면 눈이 자주 가려워요.
examples.en: If you have dry eye syndrome, your eyes itch often.
I heard he hurt his eyeball in an accident.
Something got into my eye, so I went to the hospital.

explain: 일상에서는 '눈'이라고 하고, '안구'는 눈알이라는 신체 부분을 정확하게 말할 때 써요. 병원과 건강 이야기에서 '안구 건조증', '안구 운동'처럼 굳은 말로 자주 나와요.
explain_en: In daily speech people just say '눈'. '안구' names the eyeball itself and appears in medical or health contexts in set phrases like '안구 건조증' (dry eye) and '안구 운동' (eye exercise).

examples.en: This company is famous for software engineering.
I want to major in engineering at university.

examples.ko: 엔지니어링 팀이 새 제품을 만들고 있어요.
examples.en: The engineering team is building a new product.
I got a job at a construction engineering firm.
Engineering requires a lot of math.

examples.ko: 그 회사 이름에 엔지니어링이 들어 있어요.
examples.en: The word engineering is in that company's name.

explain: 학문 이름은 '공학'이고, '엔지니어링'은 회사 이름이나 업계에서 더 많이 써요. 사람은 '엔지니어'라고 불러요. 혼자 쓰기보다 '소프트웨어 엔지니어링', '건설 엔지니어링'처럼 앞에 분야가 붙어요.
explain_en: The academic field is '공학', while '엔지니어링' is used more in company names and industry talk. A person is an '엔지니어'. It usually comes with a field before it, like '소프트웨어 엔지니어링' or '건설 엔지니어링'.

examples.ko: 의사가 이 병은 완치할 수 있다고 했어요.
examples.en: The doctor said this illness can be completely cured.
Grandfather fully recovered from pneumonia and left the hospital.

examples.ko: 큰 병은 완치하는 데 몇 년이 걸리기도 해요.
examples.en: For a serious illness, it can take years to be fully cured.

examples.ko: 완치해도 정기 검사는 계속 받아야 해요.
examples.en: Even after full recovery, you must keep getting regular checkups.
I heard the story of a person who beat cancer completely.
My friend has finally fully recovered.

explain: '낫다'는 아프던 것이 좋아질 때 일상에서 두루 쓰고, '완치하다'는 병이 완전히 없어질 때 병원이나 뉴스에서 써요. '완치되다'도 많이 써요. 치료가 다 끝났다는 느낌이라서 가벼운 증상에는 거의 안 써요.
explain_en: '낫다' is the everyday word for getting better; '완치하다' means a disease is completely gone and appears in hospitals and news. '완치되다' is also common. It implies treatment is finished, so it is rarely used for minor symptoms.

examples.ko: 장학 제도 덕분에 학비를 걱정하지 않아요.
examples.en: Thanks to the scholarship system, I do not worry about tuition.
My younger sibling got a scholarship for good grades.
A scholarship foundation is helping students.
To become a scholarship student, you need good grades.
The scholarship application deadline is tomorrow.
The company supports students through a scholarship program.

explain: '장학'은 혼자 쓰기보다 뒤에 말이 붙어 '장학금', '장학생', '장학 재단'으로 써요. 돈 이야기는 '장학금'이 훨씬 자연스러워요. '장학금을 받다', '장학생이 되다'처럼 동사와 같이 외워 두세요.
explain_en: '장학' rarely stands alone; it combines into '장학금' (scholarship money), '장학생' (scholarship student), and '장학 재단'. For money, '장학금' is far more natural. Learn it with verbs: '장학금을 받다', '장학생이 되다'.

en: transfer schools; get transferred to another school

examples.en: I am transferring to another school next month.
My friend transferred to a school in Busan.

examples.ko: 전학하면 새 친구를 사귀어야 해서 걱정돼요.
examples.en: If I transfer, I have to make new friends, so I am worried.
I was very nervous on my first day after transferring.

examples.ko: 내년에 전학할 거라서 이사 준비를 해요.
examples.en: I am going to transfer next year, so I am preparing to move.
I wrote a letter to the friend who is transferring.

explain: 초·중·고등학교에서 다른 학교로 옮길 때 써요. 대학교에서 옮기는 것은 보통 '편입하다'라고 해요. 같은 학교 안에서 반을 바꾸는 것과도 달라요. '~(으)로 전학하다', '전학을 가다/오다'로 써요.
explain_en: Used for moving to another school at the elementary, middle, or high school level. For universities, people usually say '편입하다'. It is also different from changing classes within one school. Use '~(으)로 전학하다' or '전학을 가다/오다'.

examples.en: The teaching assistant handed out the class materials.
If you have a question, ask the teaching assistant.
My older brother works as a teaching assistant in graduate school.
Thanks to the teaching assistant, I finished my homework well.
A teaching assistant helps the professor with work.
They say the lab is hiring a new teaching assistant.

explain: 대학이나 학원에서 교수님이나 강사를 도와주는 사람이에요. 직접 부를 때는 '조교님'이라고 해요. 선생님과 달리 수업을 맡기보다 자료 준비, 채점, 질문 응답을 돕는 보조 역할이 중심이에요.
explain_en: A person who assists the professor or instructor at a university or academy. You address them as '조교님'. Unlike a teacher, they mostly support with materials, grading, and answering questions rather than leading the class.

en: adviser; staff member who advises a leader

examples.en: The president's advisers held an emergency meeting.

examples.ko: 좋은 참모가 있으면 리더가 더 잘 결정해요.
examples.en: With good advisers, a leader decides better.
He is an adviser who is like the boss's right hand.

examples.ko: 선거 캠프의 참모로 일한 적이 있어요.
examples.en: I once worked as an adviser on an election campaign.
I changed the plan after hearing my adviser.
The advisory staff held a meeting all night.

explain: '비서'는 일정과 문서를 챙기는 사람이고, '참모'는 방향과 전략에 대해 조언하는 사람이에요. 정치·군대·회사 뉴스에서 주로 쓰고, 일상 대화에서는 비유로만 써요. 여러 명이면 '참모진'이라고 해요.
explain_en: A '비서' manages schedules and documents; a '참모' advises on direction and strategy. It mainly appears in political, military, and corporate news, and in daily talk only figuratively. A group of them is '참모진'.

examples.en: I saw a portrait of a king at the art museum.

examples.ko: 거리 화가가 제 초상화를 그려 줬어요.
examples.en: A street artist drew my portrait.
A portrait of my grandmother hangs on the wall.
It is hard to draw a portrait that looks like the person.
Who is the person in this portrait?
I met a painter famous for portraits.

explain: 사진은 '찍다', 초상화는 '그리다'라서 같이 쓰는 동사가 달라요. '초상화를 그리다', '초상화가 걸리다'처럼 써요. 얼굴 사진은 '증명사진'이나 '프로필 사진'이라고 해요.
explain_en: You '찍다' (take) a photo but '그리다' (draw) a portrait, so the verbs differ: '초상화를 그리다', '초상화가 걸리다'. A face photo is called a '증명사진' (ID photo) or '프로필 사진' (profile picture).

examples.ko: 칼날이 무뎌서 야채가 잘 안 썰려요.
examples.en: The blade is dull, so vegetables do not cut well.
It is dangerous to touch the blade.

examples.ko: 새 칼날로 바꿨더니 종이가 잘 잘려요.
examples.en: After switching to a new blade, paper cuts well.
This blade is very sharp.
The child cut a hand on the blade.
The tip of the blade broke off.

explain: '칼'은 도구 전체이고 '칼날'은 자르는 얇은 부분이에요. 손잡이는 '칼자루'라고 해요. 날이 잘 들면 '날카롭다', 잘 안 들면 '무디다'를 써요.
explain_en: '칼' is the whole knife and '칼날' is the thin cutting part. The handle is '칼자루'. A blade that cuts well is '날카롭다' (sharp); one that does not is '무디다' (dull).

examples.en: The coating on this frying pan has peeled off.
If you laminate paper, it does not get wet.
I laminated my student ID and have used it for a long time.
A laminated menu is easy to wipe clean.
Coating wears off over time.
Thanks to the shiny coating, the photo lasts long.

explain: 물건 이야기에서 '코팅이 벗겨지다', '코팅하다'로 자주 써요. 같은 일을 '입히다'로 풀어 말할 수도 있지만 대화에서는 보통 '코팅'을 그대로 써요. 머리나 손톱 관리 이야기에서도 '코팅한다'고 해요.
explain_en: For objects you often hear '코팅이 벗겨지다' (the coating peels) and '코팅하다'. It could be described with '입히다', but in conversation people just say '코팅'. It also appears in hair and nail care.

examples.en: The two of them are the best duo.
Our duo always goes around together.

examples.ko: 그 코미디 콤비를 모르는 사람이 없어요.
examples.en: There is nobody who does not know that comedy duo.

examples.ko: 형이랑 동생이 콤비가 되어 가게를 열었어요.
examples.en: The older and younger brothers teamed up and opened a shop.

examples.ko: 노래와 춤 실력이 좋아서 콤비로 데뷔했어요.
examples.en: They debuted as a duo because both sing and dance well.
The teamwork between the two was really cool.

explain: '친구'나 '짝'과 달리 같이 일하거나 활동할 때 호흡이 잘 맞는 두 사람에게 써요. 코미디언, 운동선수, 가수 이야기에 자주 나와요. 세 명 이상에게는 쓰지 않고 '팀'이라고 해요.
explain_en: Unlike '친구' or '짝', it is for two people who work or perform well together. It often appears for comedians, athletes, and singers. For three or more people, say '팀' instead.

examples.en: When sunlight passes through a prism, rainbow colors appear.
We did a prism experiment in science class.
A prism is a triangular shape made of glass.

examples.ko: 책상 위 프리즘이 빛을 여러 색으로 나눠요.
examples.en: The prism on the desk splits light into many colors.
The children made a rainbow with a prism.
The light shining through the prism spread over the wall.

explain: 과학 수업에서 빛을 여러 색으로 나눌 때 나오는 도구예요. '프리즘을 통과하다'처럼 써요. 일상 대화에서는 거의 안 쓰고, 관점을 비유하는 글에서 드물게 나와요.
explain_en: The tool in science class that splits light into colors. You say '프리즘을 통과하다'. It is rare in everyday speech and appears only occasionally as a metaphor for a point of view in writing.

examples.en: I wore skull makeup on Halloween.
I saw an old skull at the museum.

examples.ko: 해골 모양 반지는 저한테 안 어울려요.
examples.en: A skull-shaped ring does not suit me.
I was startled when a skeleton suddenly appeared in the movie.

examples.ko: 독이 있다는 표시로 해골 그림을 붙여요.
examples.en: They put a skull picture to show something is poisonous.

examples.ko: 며칠 못 자서 얼굴이 해골 같아요.
examples.en: I could not sleep for days, so my face looks like a skull.

explain: '뼈'는 몸속의 뼈 하나하나이고, '해골'은 죽은 사람이나 동물의 머리뼈, 또는 뼈대 전체예요. 장난스럽게 '얼굴이 해골 같다'고 하면 많이 말랐다는 뜻이에요. 무서운 분위기의 말이라서 격식 있는 자리에는 잘 안 써요.
explain_en: '뼈' is each bone in the body, while '해골' is the skull or the whole skeleton of a dead person or animal. Jokingly saying '얼굴이 해골 같다' means someone looks very thin. It has a creepy feel, so it is rarely used in formal settings.

en: sponsor; provide goods or funds in return for publicity

examples.en: A company sponsored this concert.
The sponsoring company's name appears on the screen.
A famous brand provides the costumes for the drama.

examples.ko: 가게 사장님이 행사 상품을 협찬해 주셨어요.
examples.en: The shop owner kindly donated prizes for the event.

examples.ko: 우리 학교 축제를 협찬할 회사를 찾고 있어요.
examples.en: We are looking for a company to sponsor our school festival.
I thank the people who sponsored the event.

explain: '후원하다'는 돈이나 도움을 주며 응원하는 것이고, '협찬하다'는 회사가 물건이나 돈을 대 주고 대신 이름을 알리는 거래의 느낌이 있어요. 방송 자막의 '의상 협찬'처럼 방송·행사에서 자주 보여요.
explain_en: '후원하다' is giving money or help to support someone; '협찬하다' has a business-exchange feel, where a company provides goods or funds in return for publicity. You often see it in broadcast credits like '의상 협찬' (costumes provided by).

examples.ko: 작은 실수를 간과하면 나중에 큰 문제가 돼요.
examples.en: If you overlook a small mistake, it becomes a big problem later.

examples.ko: 이 점은 절대 간과할 수 없어요.
examples.en: We absolutely cannot overlook this point.
People overlooked the importance of safety.

examples.ko: 중요한 사실을 간과한 채 결정하면 안 돼요.
examples.en: You should not decide while overlooking an important fact.
Please do not overlook that problem.

examples.ko: 간과하기 쉬운 부분을 한 번 더 확인해요.
examples.en: We check once more the parts that are easy to overlook.

explain: '간과'는 대부분 '간과하다'로 써요. '간과할 수 없다', '간과하기 쉽다'처럼 '중요한데 보지 못하고 지나친다'는 느낌이에요. 말할 때는 '놓치다'가 더 쉽고, '간과하다'는 글·발표·뉴스에서 많이 써요.
explain_en: '간과' is mostly used as the verb '간과하다', in patterns like '간과할 수 없다' and '간과하기 쉽다', meaning missing something that is actually important. '놓치다' is easier in speech; '간과하다' is common in writing, presentations, and news.

examples.en: A robber took money from the shop by force.

examples.ko: 그 나라는 이웃 나라의 땅을 강탈했어요.
examples.en: That country seized a neighboring country's land by force.
The news says they caught the man who snatched the bag.
I felt as if my childhood dream had been taken away.
Taking others' belongings by force is a crime.
The police stopped a plan to rob the cash.

explain: '빼앗다'는 일상에서 두루 쓰고, '강탈하다'는 힘이나 폭력으로 억지로 빼앗을 때 쓰는 강한 말이라 뉴스나 역사 이야기에 나와요. '훔치다'는 몰래 가져가는 것이라 달라요. 피해를 입은 쪽은 '강탈당하다'를 써요.
explain_en: '빼앗다' is the general word; '강탈하다' is a strong word for taking by force or violence, used in news and history. '훔치다' means taking secretly, so it differs. The victim's side uses '강탈당하다'.

examples.ko: 두 팀의 실력 갭이 너무 커요.
examples.en: The skill gap between the two teams is too big.

examples.ko: 세대 갭 때문에 부모님과 자주 부딪혀요.
examples.en: I often clash with my parents because of the generation gap.
I want to reduce the gap between my words and actions.
The gap between ideals and reality is bigger than I thought.

examples.ko: 월급 갭이 너무 커서 이직을 포기했어요.
examples.en: The pay gap was so big that I gave up on changing jobs.

examples.ko: 영어와 한국어 사이의 갭으로 번역이 어려워요.
examples.en: Translation is hard because of the gap between English and Korean.

explain: '차이'보다 격차나 틈이 크다는 느낌이 강해서 '실력 갭', '세대 갭'처럼 앞에 말이 붙어요. 말할 때 편하게 쓰는 말이고, 글이나 발표에서는 '격차'가 더 정중해요.
explain_en: Compared with '차이' (difference), '갭' stresses a large divide, and a word usually comes before it: '실력 갭', '세대 갭'. It is casual spoken style; in writing or presentations '격차' sounds more formal.

examples.en: The trial hearing opens tomorrow morning.
A witness spoke at the hearing.
The hearing date was postponed by a month.
The lawyer is preparing for the hearing.

examples.ko: 공판은 많은 사람이 볼 수 있는 법정에서 열려요.
examples.en: A public hearing is held in a courtroom that many people can watch.
The news reported on the first hearing.

explain: '재판'은 법원이 판단하는 일 전체이고, '공판'은 그중 법정에서 공개로 주장을 듣고 증거를 확인하는 단계예요. 뉴스에서 '첫 공판', '공판이 열리다'로 많이 나오고, 일상 대화에서는 보통 '재판'이라고 해요.
explain_en: '재판' is the whole judging process by a court; '공판' is the stage in open court where arguments are heard and evidence checked. In the news you see '첫 공판' and '공판이 열리다'; in everyday talk people just say '재판'.

examples.en: The darling of our house is the puppy.
The youngest is the family's darling.
My younger sibling smiles like a little cutie.
Grandmother calls me her darling.
The class darling was absent today.
I bought a new toy for my little darling.

explain: '애교쟁이'는 애교를 잘 부리는 사람이고, '귀염둥이'는 귀여워서 사랑받는 사람이에요. 아이와 반려동물에게 쓰고, 어른에게 쓰면 놀리는 느낌이 있어요.
explain_en: An '애교쟁이' is someone who acts charmingly; a '귀염둥이' is someone loved for being cute. It is used for children and pets, and said to an adult it can sound teasing.

examples.en: In winter the sun rises in the southeast.
A typhoon is coming up from the southeast.
My house is to the southeast of the school.

examples.ko: 이 방은 남동향이라 아침 해가 잘 들어요.
examples.en: This room faces southeast, so it gets morning sun well.
On the map, go toward the southeast.
A southeast wind is blowing, so it is humid.

explain: 방향은 보통 '남동쪽'처럼 '쪽'을 붙여 말해요. '동남'도 같은 방향이지만 '동남아시아'처럼 굳은 말은 '동남'을 써요. 집이 해가 아침에 드는 방향일 때 '남동향'이라는 말을 많이 써요.
explain_en: Directions are usually said with '쪽', as in '남동쪽'. '동남' means the same direction, but set terms like '동남아시아' use '동남'. For homes that get morning sun, '남동향' is commonly used.

examples.ko: 동북 지방은 겨울에 눈이 많이 와요.
examples.en: The northeast region gets a lot of snow in winter.
I want to travel to the northeast of China.
Korea is in Northeast Asia.
The typhoon is moving up toward the northeast.
A northeast wind is blowing, so it is chilly.
My neighborhood has a mountain to the northeast.

explain: '북동'도 같은 방향이에요. '동북아시아', '동북 지방'처럼 굳은 말은 '동북'을 써요. 중국 이야기에서 '동북 지방'은 보통 북동쪽에 있는 지역을 가리켜요.
explain_en: '북동' is the same direction, but set terms like '동북아시아' and '동북 지방' use '동북'. In talk about China, '동북 지방' refers to the region in the northeast.

examples.en: I went into a maze at the amusement park and got lost.
The hallways of this building are like a maze.
The children are solving a maze puzzle.

examples.ko: 미로의 출구를 찾는 데 한 시간이 걸렸어요.
examples.en: It took an hour to find the exit of the maze.
The market alleys are as complicated as a maze.

examples.ko: 이 미로에서 빠져나갈 길이 안 보여요.
examples.en: I cannot see a way out of this maze.

explain: 놀이공원 시설뿐 아니라 '미로 같은 골목'처럼 복잡해서 헤매는 곳이나 상황을 비유할 때도 많이 써요. '길을 잃다', '미로를 빠져나가다'와 같이 쓰면 자연스러워요.
explain_en: Besides the amusement-park attraction, it is often a metaphor for a confusing place or situation, as in '미로 같은 골목'. It sounds natural with '길을 잃다' and '미로를 빠져나가다'.

examples.en: I went on a mountain hike with friends on the weekend.
It rained during the hike, so we came down.
This hike takes about three hours.
Gloves are a must for winter hikes.
I checked the hiking course in advance.
My father goes to a hiking club every month.

explain: '등산'과 거의 같지만 '산행'은 산길을 걷는 일정 전체의 느낌이 있어서 '산행 코스', '산행 모임'처럼 써요. 일상에서는 '등산'이 더 흔하고, 산악회 안내문이나 후기에서 '산행'이 자주 보여요.
explain_en: Nearly the same as '등산', but '산행' feels like the whole trek along mountain paths, so you get '산행 코스' and '산행 모임'. '등산' is more common in daily talk; '산행' shows up in hiking-club notices and trip reports.

examples.en: I hike every Sunday.
We started hiking at dawn.
It is raining, so we are not hiking today.
I took many photos while hiking with friends.

examples.ko: 겨울에 산행할 때는 따뜻하게 입어야 해요.
examples.en: When hiking in winter, you should dress warmly.
Yesterday I went hiking on Seoraksan.

explain: '등산하다'와 비슷하지만 말투가 조금 더 글 같아요. 보통은 '산에 가다', '등산하다'라고 하고, '산행하다'는 산악회 후기나 방송에서 들어요. '설악산을 산행하다'처럼 산 이름을 목적어로 쓸 수 있어요.
explain_en: Similar to '등산하다' but a bit more written in tone. People usually say '산에 가다' or '등산하다'; '산행하다' appears in hiking-club reports and broadcasts. The mountain name can be the object: '설악산을 산행하다'.

examples.ko: 오늘 야구장에서 유명한 배우가 시구를 해요.
examples.en: A famous actor throws the first pitch at the ballpark today.
The first pitch is thrown before the game starts.
It was cute to see a young fan throw the first pitch.
The singer's first pitch fell onto the ground.
After the first pitch, we took photos with the players.
I wonder who is throwing the first pitch this time.

explain: '시구하다', '시구를 하다' 둘 다 써요. 공을 던지면 '시구', 방망이를 휘두르면 '시타', 공을 받으면 '시포'라고 해요. 보통 연예인이나 어린이 팬이 맡고, 뉴스에도 자주 나와요.
explain_en: Both '시구하다' and '시구를 하다' are used. Throwing is '시구', swinging the bat is '시타', and catching is '시포'. Celebrities or young fans usually do it, and it often makes the news.

examples.en: I felt relieved after seeing the exam result.
Everyone was relieved to hear the child was safe.

examples.ko: 길을 찾은 뒤에야 안도할 수 있었어요.
examples.en: I could only feel relieved after finding the way.
My parents felt relieved at the news that I had arrived.
When the rain stopped, people had relieved looks.
He took a deep breath, feeling relieved.

explain: '다행이다'는 일이 잘 풀려서 좋다는 마음이고, '안도하다'는 걱정하던 일이 끝나서 마음이 놓이는 모습을 말해요. 글이나 뉴스에서 많이 쓰고, 말할 때는 '마음이 놓이다'가 더 자연스러워요.

phrases.example: 합격 소식을 듣고 안도의 한숨을 쉬었어요.
phrases.nuance_ko: 걱정이 끝났을 때 숨을 길게 내쉬는 모습으로 말해요. 실제 한숨이 아니어도 마음이 놓였다는 뜻으로 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Describes the long breath you let out when a worry ends. It can be used even without an actual sigh, to mean you feel relieved.

explain_en: '다행이다' is feeling glad that things turned out well; '안도하다' describes the moment your mind settles because a worry is over. It is common in writing and news; in speech '마음이 놓이다' is more natural.

examples.en: The mermaid in the fairy tale lives in the sea.
Do you know the story of the little mermaid?
The child sleeps holding a mermaid doll.
I want to swim as well as a mermaid.
A mermaid statue stands at the beach.
I watched a movie where a mermaid becomes a human.

explain: 대부분 동화 '인어공주'로 접하는 말이에요. 수영을 아주 잘하는 사람을 '인어 같다'고 비유하기도 해요. 가장 흔한 짝말은 '인어공주', '인어 동상'이에요.
explain_en: Most people meet this word through the fairy tale '인어공주' (The Little Mermaid). Someone who swims very well can be called '인어 같다'. Common pairings are '인어공주' and '인어 동상'.

examples.en: I take pride in my cooking skills.
He believed with pride that he was the best in the country.

examples.ko: 자기 일을 자부하는 사람은 쉽게 포기하지 않아요.
examples.en: People who take pride in their work do not give up easily.
The team members can be proud of this result.
That company takes pride in its technology.
You can fairly say with pride that you worked harder than anyone.

explain: '자랑하다'는 남에게 보여 주며 말하는 것이고, '자부하다'는 스스로 속으로 당당하다고 믿는 것이에요. '~을 자부하다', '~에 자부심을 가지다'로 쓰고, '자부심'이라는 명사도 자주 써요. 말투가 조금 딱딱해서 글이나 인터뷰에서 많이 보여요.
explain_en: '자랑하다' is showing off to others; '자부하다' is quietly and confidently believing in yourself. Use '~을 자부하다' or '~에 자부심을 가지다'; the noun '자부심' is common too. It sounds a bit stiff and shows up in writing and interviews.

examples.en: I said goodbye to my family at the airport.
I have to part from a friend I was with for a long time.
Tears came at the moment we parted.

examples.ko: 우리는 역에서 작별하고 각자 집으로 갔어요.
examples.en: We said farewell at the station and went to our own homes.
When it was time to say goodbye, the child cried.

examples.ko: 오래된 집과 작별하며 마지막 사진을 찍었어요.
examples.en: I took a last photo as I said farewell to the old house.

explain: '헤어지다'는 일상에서 두루 쓰고 연인에게도 써요. '작별하다'는 오랫동안 못 만날 사람이나 장소에 정식으로 인사하는 느낌이라 글이나 뉴스에 많아요. 말로는 '작별 인사를 하다'가 더 흔해요.
explain_en: '헤어지다' is the everyday word and also covers couples breaking up. '작별하다' feels like a formal goodbye to someone or somewhere you will not see for a long time, common in writing and news. In speech '작별 인사를 하다' is more usual.

examples.en: The past life I saw in a dream was so vivid.
Some people believe in past lives.
Those two must have been connected since a past life.
My friend must have been a cat in a past life.
I watched a drama with a past-life story.
It is a story about a child with memories of a past life.

explain: 믿는지와 상관없이 일상 대화에서 비유로 자주 써요. 이상하게 잘 맞는 사람에게 '전생에 무슨 사이였을까'라고 농담해요. '전생'의 반대인 '내생'은 거의 안 쓰고, '이번 생'과 '다음 생'을 많이 말해요.

phrases.example: 이런 좋은 사람들을 만나다니 전생에 나라를 구했나 봐요.
phrases.en: I must have saved a country in a past life
phrases.nuance_ko: 운이 아주 좋을 때 감탄하며 말해요. 정말 전생을 말하는 게 아니라 복이 많다는 뜻이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: An exclamation when you are very lucky. It is not about a real past life, just meaning you have great fortune.
phrases.en_equiv: I must have done something great in a past life

explain_en: Whether or not people believe in it, it is often used figuratively in daily talk. For someone you click with strangely well, you joke '전생에 무슨 사이였을까' (what were we in a past life?). The opposite '내생' is rarely used; people say '이번 생' and '다음 생'.

examples.en: The bus is stopped at the bus stop.
The stopping time is usually one minute.

examples.ko: 이 도로에서는 정차를 할 수 없어요.
examples.en: You cannot stop on this road.
The train stops at Busan Station and then departs.
I paid a fine for illegal stopping.

examples.ko: 갑자기 정차하는 바람에 몸이 앞으로 쏠렸어요.
examples.en: The vehicle stopped suddenly, so my body lurched forward.

explain: '정차'는 차가 잠깐 서는 것, '주차'는 차를 세워 두고 자리를 비우는 것이라 달라요. 안내 방송과 표지판에 자주 나오고 '정차 금지', '정차 중'처럼 굳은 말로 알아 두세요. 일상에서 멈추는 건 '서다'를 써요.
explain_en: '정차' is a vehicle stopping briefly; '주차' is leaving a parked vehicle, so they differ. It appears in announcements and road signs in fixed phrases like '정차 금지' and '정차 중'. In daily speech, 'to stop' is '서다'.

examples.en: The bus stops at every stop.

examples.ko: 이 급행 열차는 작은 역에는 정차하지 않아요.
examples.en: This express train does not stop at small stations.
A taxi stopped in front of the building.
We will stop for a moment because of the signal.
Do not open the door while it is stopped.
I was startled when the car ahead suddenly stopped.

explain: '서다'와 '멈추다'는 일상 말이고, '정차하다'는 버스·기차·택시 안내에서 쓰는 말이에요. '~에 정차하다'로 쓰고 급행 열차는 '정차하지 않는다'고 안내해요. 사람이 걷다가 멈추는 건 '정차'라고 하지 않아요.
explain_en: '서다' and '멈추다' are everyday words; '정차하다' is the word used in bus, train, and taxi announcements. Use '~에 정차하다'; express trains 'do not stop' (정차하지 않는다). It is not used for a person who stops while walking.

en: steering wheel; handlebars (not a door handle)

examples.ko: 운전할 때는 핸들을 두 손으로 잡으세요.
examples.en: When driving, hold the steering wheel with both hands.
The steering wheel on this car is too heavy.
I swerved suddenly and avoided an accident.
I hung my bag on the bicycle handlebars.

examples.ko: 핸들 위치를 내 키에 맞게 조절했어요.
examples.en: I adjusted the steering wheel position to my height.
The steering wheel is made of leather, so it is not slippery.

explain: 한국어 '핸들'은 자동차 운전대와 자전거·오토바이의 손잡이 막대를 말해요. 영어 handle처럼 문이나 가방의 손잡이를 '핸들'이라고 하면 어색하고, 그때는 '손잡이'라고 해요. '핸들을 잡다', '핸들을 꺾다'처럼 써요.
explain_en: Korean '핸들' means a car's steering wheel or the handlebars of a bicycle or motorbike. Calling a door or bag handle a '핸들' is wrong; that is '손잡이'. Use it as '핸들을 잡다' or '핸들을 꺾다'.

examples.en: I bought flowers at a flower shop as a gift for Parents' Day.

examples.ko: 우리 동네 화원은 아침 일찍 문을 열어요.
examples.en: The flower shop in my neighborhood opens early in the morning.

examples.ko: 화원 주인이 꽃 이름을 알려 줬어요.
examples.en: The flower shop owner told me the flowers' names.
I stopped by the flower shop and bought a potted plant.
They say the old flower shop is closing.

examples.ko: 학교 앞 화원 덕분에 길이 향기로워요.
examples.en: Thanks to the flower shop in front of the school, the street smells nice.

explain: 일상에서는 '꽃집'이 훨씬 흔하고, '화원'은 가게 간판이나 이름에서 자주 보여요. 꽃을 가꾸어 보여 주는 정원을 가리킬 때도 있지만 요즘은 꽃 가게로 더 많이 써요. 글에서는 '화원'이 조금 격식 있게 들려요.
explain_en: In daily talk '꽃집' is far more common; '화원' shows up on shop signs and names. It can mean a cultivated flower garden, but nowadays it mostly means a flower shop. In writing it sounds a little more formal.

examples.en: My friend changed their name this year.

examples.ko: 법원에서 허락을 받아야 개명할 수 있어요.
examples.en: You can change your name only with the court's permission.
After changing my name, I am called by the new one.
My name is hard, so I plan to change it.
The singer became more famous after changing their name.
I looked into the documents needed to change my name.

explain: 법적으로 이름을 바꿀 때는 '개명하다'를 써요. '이름을 개명하다'는 뜻이 겹쳐서 어색하니 '개명하다'만 쓰는 게 자연스러워요. 가수나 배우가 활동 이름을 바꾸는 건 '예명을 바꾸다'라고 해요.
explain_en: Use '개명하다' for a legal name change. '이름을 개명하다' repeats the meaning and sounds awkward, so just say '개명하다'. For a singer or actor changing a stage name, say '예명을 바꾸다'.

examples.en: This broadcaster is state-run.
State-run companies are operated by the government.
State-run hospitals tend to have low fees.
That country runs its railways as a state enterprise.
In the past, many companies were state-run.

examples.ko: 그 나라의 국영 방송 뉴스를 봤어요.
examples.en: I watched the news on that country's state broadcaster.

explain: 반대말은 '민영'이고, '국영 기업', '국영 방송'처럼 뒤의 말을 꾸며요. 한국의 KBS처럼 공공이 운영하는 방송은 '국영'이 아니라 '공영 방송'이라고 해요. 다른 나라나 옛날 이야기에서 자주 나오는 말이에요.
explain_en: The opposite is '민영', and it modifies the next word: '국영 기업', '국영 방송'. A publicly run broadcaster like Korea's KBS is called '공영 방송', not '국영'. It often comes up when talking about other countries or the past.
